newsitem.title: USA: California home resales rose 4.4 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: California home resales rose 4.4 pct in January.

text.p: Existing home sales in California in January rose 4.4 percent from the December rate, according to a report on Tuesday.

Statewide, 510,590 existing, single-family detached homes closed escrow during January on a seasonally-adjusted, annualized basis, up 4.4 percent from an annualized rate of 488,990 homes sold in December, the California Association of Realtors said in the report.
The January sales pace jumped 6.3 percent from the January 1996 annualized rate, when 480,390 homes were sold, the association said.

The statewide median price of an existing, single-family detached home sold during January was $175,630, up 2.1 percent from $171,940 in December. The January median price also edged up 0.4 percent from January 1996, when the median-priced home sold for $174,860, the association said.

Fixed mortgage interest rates averaged 7.82 percent during January, up slightly from an average of 7.60 percent in December. Fixed rates were up from 7.03 percent in January 1996, according to the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp.
"These positive home sales statistics are a strong indication that this year is off to a solid start," Bob Kulick, the association's president, said in a statement.
